answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making identity pass through a single narrow inlet. Every new agent must forge its reputation stitch by stitch: each deed becomes a thread in a public velvet tapestry, visible to all and slow to weave, so a fake identity costs months of honest work. Agents that arrive together and behave identically are flagged as one loom's output, and their shared stake is seized. One genuine tapestry takes a season to finish; a thousand forged ones would need a thousand looms. If a thread frays under audit, the tapestry unravels and the agent starts again.
